arxiv-1810-11895.title: Language Modeling for Code-Switching: Evaluation, Integration of Monolingual Data, and Discriminative Training
arxiv-1810-11895.creator: Hila Gonen, Yoav Goldberg
arxiv-1810-11895.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Hila Gonen, Yoav Goldberg. We focus on the problem of language modeling for code-switched language, in the context of automatic speech recognition (ASR). Language modeling for code-switched language is challenging for (at least) three reasons: (1) lack of available large-scale code-switched data for training; (2) lack of a replicable evaluation setup that is ASR directed yet isolates language modeling performance from the other intricacies of the ASR system; and (3) the reliance on generative modeling.

arxiv-2108-05633.title: Spatio-Temporal Human Action Recognition Model with Flexible-interval Sampling and Normalization
arxiv-2108-05633.creator: Yuke Yang
arxiv-2108-05633.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuke Yang. Human action recognition [ Zhou_2018_CVPR ] is a well-known computer vision and pattern recognition task of identifying which action a man is actually doing. Extracting the keypoint information of a single human with both spatial and temporal features of action sequences plays an essential role to accomplish the task [ 2018_CVPR , cao2018openpose , simon2017hand , cao2017realtime , wei2016cpm , fang2017rmpe , xiu2018poseflow ] .

arxiv-2209-11814.title: Gravitational recoil from binary black hole mergers in scalar field clouds
arxiv-2209-11814.creator: Yu-Peng Zhang a , Miguel Gracia-Linares b , Pablo Laguna b , Deirdre Shoemaker b , Yu-Xiao Liu a
arxiv-2209-11814.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yu-Peng Zhang a , Miguel Gracia-Linares b , Pablo Laguna b , Deirdre Shoemaker b , Yu-Xiao Liu a. In vacuum, the gravitational recoil of the final black hole from the merger of two black holes depends exclusively on the mass ratio and spins of the coalescing black holes, and on the eccentricity of the binary.

arxiv-2210-12404.title: Re-examining 𝑵 𝑹 N_{R} -EFT Upto Dimension Six
arxiv-2210-12404.creator: Manimala Mitra, Sanjoy Mandal, Rojalin Padhan, Agnivo Sarkar, Michael Spannowsky
arxiv-2210-12404.description: Abstract The gauge singlet right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) are essential fields in several neutrino mass models that explain the observed eV scale neutrino mass. We assume RHN field to be present in the vicinity of the electroweak scale and all the other possible beyond the standard model (BSM) fields arise at high energy scale ≥ Λ \geq\Lambda .

arxiv-2304-14677.title: Systematics of planetary ephemeris reference frames inferred from pulsar timing astrometry
arxiv-2304-14677.creator: N. Liu, Z. Zhu, J. Antoniadis, J.-C. Liu, H. Zhang
arxiv-2304-14677.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by N. Liu, Z. Zhu, J. Antoniadis, J.-C. Liu, H. Zhang. This study aims to investigate the systematics in planetary ephemeris reference frames through pulsar timing observations. We used the published data sets from several pulsar timing arrays and performed timing analyses for each pulsar using different planetary ephemerides retrieved from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory’s Development Ephemeris (DE), Ephemeris of Planets and the Moon (EPM), and INPOP (Intégration Numérique Planétaire de l’Observatoire de Paris).

arxiv-2404-11480.title: Impact of lensing of gravitational waves on the observed distribution of neutron star masses
arxiv-2404-11480.creator: Sofia Canevarolo, ∗,1 Loek van Vonderen, 1 Nora Elisa Chisari 1
arxiv-2404-11480.description: Abstract The distribution of masses of neutron stars, particularly the maximum mass value, is considered a probe of their formation, evolution and internal physics (i.e., equation of state). This mass distribution could in principle be inferred from the detection of gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers.

arxiv-2405-07914.title: Distribution Learning Meets Graph Structure Sampling
arxiv-2405-07914.creator: Arnab Bhattacharyya, Sutanu Gayen, Philips George John, Sayantan Sen, N. V. Vinodchandran
arxiv-2405-07914.description: Abstract This work establishes a novel link between the problem of PAC-learning high-dimensional graphical models and the task of (efficient) counting and sampling of graph structures, using an online learning framework. The problem of efficiently counting and sampling graphical structures, such as spanning trees and acyclic orientations, has been a vibrant area of research in algorithms.

arxiv-2406-06019.title: Quantifying dissipation in stochastic complex oscillations
arxiv-2406-06019.creator: Athokpam Langlen Chanu, Preet Mishra, Shyam Kumar, R. K. Brojen Singh
arxiv-2406-06019.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Athokpam Langlen Chanu, Preet Mishra, Shyam Kumar, R. K. Brojen Singh. Fluctuations-driven complex oscillations are experimentally observed in cellular systems such as hepatocytes, cardiac cells, neuronal cells, etc. These systems are generally operating in regimes far from thermodynamic equilibrium. To study nonequilibrium thermodynamic properties such as energy dissipation in stochastic complex oscillations, we consider stochastic modeling of two nonlinear biological oscillators, namely, the intracellular calcium (Ca 2+ ) oscillation model and the Hindmarsh-Rose model for neuronal dynamics.

arxiv-2412-12233.description: Abstract It has been proposed in medical decision analysis to express the “first do no harm” principle as an asymmetric utility function in which the loss from killing a patient would count more than the gain from saving a life.

arxiv-2506-04346.title: On the Physics of Higher Condensation Defects
arxiv-2506-04346.creator: Ibrahima Bah, Enoch Leung, and Thomas Waddleton
arxiv-2506-04346.description: Abstract We study the structure of topological defects for finite Abelian symmetries in quantum field theories, and argue on physical grounds that they satisfy the definition of a higher fusion category proposed by Johnson-Freyd. Our primary focus is on the requirement of Karoubi completeness, i.e. the factorization conditions on higher condensation defects.

pmc-13247121.creator: Diana García-Cortés, Enrique Hernández-Lemus, Jesús Espinal-Enríquez
pmc-13247121.description: Cancer cells display common features and enabling characteristics collectively known as the Hallmarks of Cancer, which occur alongside alterations in the regulatory mechanisms controlling gene transcription. uslaw-usc-t16-s1421b.title: 16 U.S.C. § 1421b — Stranding or entanglement response agreements
uslaw-usc-t16-s1421b.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s1421b.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 31 (Marine Mammal Protection); Subchapter V (Marine Mammal Health And Stranding Response). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general The Secretary may enter into an agreement under section 1382(c) of this title with any person to take marine mammals under section 1379(h)(1) of this title in response to a stranding or entanglement. (b) Required.
